purpose: This follows a root or a logarithm continuously while z moves, and shows why √z and log z cannot be single-valued and continuous on the punctured plane. A branch cut makes a choice; the Riemann surface is where the function becomes one continuous function.

stops.title: Two panes
stops.text: Left (or top): the z-plane, with the handle z, its path in blue, the violet branch point and the red cut. Right (or bottom): the followed value w in yellow and the branch value as a red ring. A red dashed line marks a jump.
stops.try: Drag z once around 0 and back to where it started. Is w where it started?

stops.title: Pick the function
stops.text: √z has two values, z^(1/n) has n, log z has infinitely many. √(z² − 1) has two branch points, −1 and +1. Changing the function starts over at the start point.
stops.try: Choose z^(1/n) with n = 3 and count the turns until w returns.

stops.title: Wind without dragging
stops.text: The angle θ is unwrapped: 360° is one full turn, so the slider from −1080° to 1080° winds z up to three times either way. |z| sets the distance from 0, kept at least 0.2.
stops.try: Slide θ from 0° to 720° and watch w.

stops.title: Turns and loops
stops.text: +1 turn and −1 turn send z once around 0. Loop that misses 0 runs a loop with 0 outside it. For √(z² − 1) the buttons loop around −1, +1, both or neither.

stops.title: Move the cut
stops.text: The branch cut is the red ray at angle α. The branch value is continuous everywhere except across it. α = 180° gives the principal branch. Moving the cut changes which sheet is called sheet 1, not the function.
stops.try: Set α = 90° and drag z across the new cut.

stops.title: The Riemann surface
stops.text: Switch the second pane to a 3D sketch of the Riemann surface: one sheet per value, glued along the red seams. The yellow point moves on it without ever jumping. Turn the surface with its slider.
stops.try: Show the surface for log z and press +1 turn.

stops.title: The readout
stops.text: The readout lists z, the turns around each branch point, the followed w, the branch value and the sheet. Each time z comes back to the start, it records the turns and the value of w.
stops.try: Compare the followed w and the branch value after one turn.

stops.title: Predict, then see
stops.text: Three predictions: commit to a choice, then the figure runs the loop and explains the result.
stops.try: Do prediction 1 before pressing any turn button.

stops.title: Practice
stops.text: Ten fixed problems: values after loops, principal values of Log, cuts, sheets, and two where you move z yourself to reach a target value. Every choice gets an explanation. Nothing is saved.

teacher: Ask for the prediction before any turn. A common misconception is that the cut is a property of the function (the negative axis). Use the cut slider to show it is a choice, and √(z² − 1) to show that a loop around both branch points changes nothing.
